content.body:
Originally a tank gun selected for economy and expediency, the QF 2 pounder quickly became one of the war's best medium AT guns. Interwar British doctrine was that machineguns were for use against infantry, and direct-fire cannons were meant to deal with tanks, so the perfect weapon would be a medium caliber gun firing high-velocity solid shot. The 2 pdr was perfect.
The carriage upon which it was mounted was ideal for high-speed travel, had 360-degree traverse as well as a full gun shield. In the early years of the war, it was capable of defeating most of the armor it faced. By the middle/end of the war it was obsolete due to the ever-increasing armor on enemy tanks.
The QF 2 pdr is an outstanding gun in Battleground Europe. It has an exceptionally flat trajectory making hits easy to score well past 500 m, the lack of high-magnification sights and range adjustment are its only shortcomings. The gun shield is good and the green color blends nicely into the terrain at any distance. The 360-degree traverse is especially welcome against the later war tanks that must be engaged from the sides or rear to have any chance of penetrating.
Engage all but the heaviest German tanks at 500 m or so, but beware that they probably have better sighting optics than you do; if you allow them the opportunity to return fire, it will be deadly. Place yourself in brush-lines where your distinctive silhouette will not be obvious.
CREW POSITIONS: 1 Commander 2 Gunner
